source.title: Minimum Insertions to Balance a Parentheses String

teaching.hint: If one right parenthesis of a closing pair has appeared, what must happen before a new opening parenthesis can begin?

solution_outline.decisive_insight: Track how many right parentheses are owed. A lone first right parenthesis of a closing pair must be completed before a new opening, and a right parenthesis with no opener forces an inserted opener.
solution_outline.approach: Scan the string with a count of owed right parentheses. An opening adds two; if it interrupts an odd outstanding debt, insert one right parenthesis first. A closing consumes one; if debt becomes negative, insert an opening and leave one right parenthesis owed. At the end, insert every remaining owed right parenthesis.
solution_outline.state_and_invariant: The debt describes closing characters still required by open pairs in a minimally repaired prefix, and the insertion count records exactly the forced repairs already made. An odd debt marks a half-completed closing token.
solution_outline.correctness: An interrupted half-token cannot be completed after a new opening while keeping its two right parentheses adjacent, so one insertion is forced. A right parenthesis with no available opener likewise forces an opening. These local repairs preserve a feasible balanced prefix with the fewest insertions; any remaining debt at the end requires exactly that many appended closers. Thus the total is necessary and sufficient.
solution_outline.complexity: O(n) time and O(1) auxiliary space for a string of length n.
solution_outline.pitfall: Treating each single right parenthesis as a full closing token gives the ordinary-parentheses answer, which is wrong here.

common_wrong_turns: Allow a new opening between the two characters of one closing token
Fail to insert an opener when debt becomes negative
Forget remaining closing debt at the end
source_fidelity_notes: The source's balanced/unbalanced examples were condensed to one contrast; two consecutive closing characters, usual nesting, insertion-only rule, and length bound were retained.
